clue.text: Pans' edges outside appear regularly overlooked; they're worn inside

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, and to carpet is to reprimand, so pans gives carpets

indicators.note: the edges go outside the next piece, wrapping round it in this clue

parts.note: the edges of a cup or wound are its lips

indicators.note: every other letter of appear is passed over, so only the alternate ones remain

explanation.surface: A cook notices the rims of the pans are being skipped at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pans' reads as cookware but is the verb to criticise. 'regularly overlooked' skips the odd letters of appear, keeping the even ones; 'outside' wraps the edges round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft carpet slippers are indoor footwear, worn around the house rather than out of doors.

clue.text: Primate conducting Mass departs energised

indicators.note: the ape conducts, that is carries, mass inside it

parts.note: an ape is a primate
M is the physics symbol for mass
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: An archbishop leading Mass leaves in a lively state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' looks like an archbishop, but it is an ape. 'conducting' puts M inside APE.
explanation.definitionFit: Amped is slang for excited or full of energy, pumped up.

clue.text: Drive forward, changing direction at end? That's correct

indicators.note: the last letter is a direction, left, and it is swapped for the opposite, right

parts.note: to propel is to drive forward

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether pushing ahead while turning at the finish is the right approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing direction at end' turns PROPEL's final L (left) into R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Proper means right or fitting, the correct way of doing things.

clue.text: Swayed A-list bloke in charge like a charm

indicators.note: swayed means moved from side to side, so these letters are shifted around

parts.note: a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: A celebrity man in charge was won over as if by a charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swayed' rearranges A-LIST as TALIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object thought to have magic powers, a lucky charm.

clue.text: Missing link's first love gutted scientist

indicators.note: only the initial letter of link is wanted here

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: the scientist is gutted, emptied of all its inner letters, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: The missing link's first discoverer was a heartbroken scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like dismayed but it strips SCIENTIST to ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lost is missing, gone from where it should be.

clue.text: Element of roof illuminated, looking up through window

indicators.note: the reversed word passes through the window pane, sitting inside it

parts.note: a pane is a sheet of glass in a window

indicators.note: in a down entry, looking up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: lit means illuminated

explanation.surface: Part of a roof lit up as someone looks up through a window.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'looking up' reads the word for illuminated from the bottom; 'through' sets the result inside the window glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantile is a curved roof tile, one of the units making up a roof.

clue.text: Kipper evident here in dish which vegetarian declines?

indicators.note: the bed is placed in the middle of the dish

parts.note: an entrée is a dish, a course of a meal
a kipper here is someone who kips, a sleeper; you see a sleeping baby in a cot

explanation.surface: Kippers are on show in a dish a vegetarian would turn down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kipper' looks like smoked fish; it is a sleeper, found in a COT. The '?' flags the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrecôte is a steak cut from between the ribs, meat that a vegetarian refuses.

clue.text: Romantic enraptured by single medium

parts.note: sent is old slang for enraptured, transported with delight
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a mentalist is someone claiming psychic powers, like a medium

explanation.surface: A romantic is spellbound by a lone spiritualist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just puts the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentimentalist indulges in tender, romantic feeling.

clue.text: Original parish has older collection of poems

indicators.note: original means newly made, so the letters are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An old parish holds an earlier anthology of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' is the anagram signal on PARISH HAS OLDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shropshire Lad is A. E. Housman's 1896 cycle of sixty-three poems.

clue.text: Food soaked by Charlie in pickle's Greek

parts.note: a sop is a piece of bread soaked in liquid

indicators.note: Charlie is placed in the middle of the word for a pickle

parts.note: a pickle is a hole, a tight spot; pickle's stands for hole's, written HOLES
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cook describes bread soaked in pickle juice by someone called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' looks like a preserve but is a predicament, a hole; 'in' sets Charlie inside it, and 'by' just places the soaked food beside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles was the ancient Athenian tragedian who wrote Oedipus Rex.

clue.text: A bit thick, Pierre's negative about sacred books

indicators.note: the French no goes round the abbreviation for the scriptures

parts.note: Pierre stands for a Frenchman, whose word for no is non
OT, the Old Testament, is a set of sacred books

explanation.surface: A Frenchman, a bit dim, says no when asked about holy scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit thick' suggests stupidity, but it is the British idiom for unacceptable behaviour; 'about' wraps the French negative round the scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British idioms for behaviour that is unreasonable or beyond what can be tolerated.

clue.text: Scarlet frock with intersecting diamonds set right

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red

indicators.note: the two words cross and share one letter, so the shared letter is written only once

parts.note: a frock is a dress
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A scarlet frock with a pattern of crossing diamond shapes is put right.
explanation.walkthrough: RED and DRESS overlap on their shared D, the diamonds, so RED DRESS loses one D.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to remedy or correct it.

clue.text: Sitcom screened — I didn't catch that one

parts.note: screened means hid, as from view
eh is what you say when you didn't hear something
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A viewer says a sitcom was shown but they missed one episode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screened' looks like broadcast but means HID. Hi-de-Hi! was a BBC sitcom set in a 1950s holiday camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-de-Hi! was a long-running British television situation comedy of the 1980s.

clue.text: Rising boxer with long hair entertains party — she's besotted

indicators.note: the reversed boxer takes in, entertains, the party
in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was the famous heavyweight boxer
a do is a party
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming long-haired boxer hosts a party for a besotted woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'Rising' reads the boxer upwards; 'entertains' then takes the party inside, and the long hair follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolatress is a woman who worships something or someone excessively, a besotted admirer.

clue.text: Spread rug to cover this?

definitions.meaning: pâté is a savoury paste spread on toast
a rug is slang for a toupee, worn to cover the top of the head

explanation.surface: A spread rug over something, and you wonder what it is hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a verb laying the rug out; it is the food. 'rug' is slang for a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: Pâté is a smooth meat or fish paste, and a pate is the crown of the head that a toupee hides.

clue.text: Sort of devil that Errol Flynn is

definitions.meaning: the ... devil is a carnivorous marsupial
Errol Flynn, the swashbuckling film star, was born in Hobart, Tasmania

explanation.surface: Errol Flynn, notorious hellraiser, is called a certain kind of devil.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at Flynn's wild reputation, but he is simply a native of Tasmania.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmanian names both the marsupial devil of that island and someone born there.

clue.text: Rider may feel that puzzles on small journey occasionally needed

indicators.note: puzzles comes on, that is after, the letter for small

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to addle someone is to confuse or puzzle them

indicators.note: only some of the letters of journey are used, every other one

explanation.surface: Someone baffled is told a short trip will sometimes be required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters of JOURNEY, ORE. 'needed' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse rider who has spent long hours in the saddle gets sore and chafed.

clue.text: Islander living here welcomes keyboard one forwarded

parts.note: hi is a greeting or welcome, and his is its plural

indicators.note: the numeral one is moved further along the word for the keyboard

parts.note: a pianola is a self-playing piano, a keyboard instrument

explanation.surface: An islander at home greets someone and sends a keyboard on ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomes' is a plural noun, greetings, not a verb. 'one forwarded' moves the I (one) of the keyboard two places further along.
explanation.definitionFit: Hispaniola is the Caribbean island shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic, home to islanders.

clue.text: Sterling left in disarray, without a goal

parts.note: sterling means excellent, A1, written here as AI

indicators.note: the letter for left goes in the middle of the disarray

parts.note: a mess is disarray

explanation.surface: A footballer named Sterling is left in a mess, having failed to score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sterling' looks like the footballer or the currency; it means first-rate, A1, used as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimless means lacking any purpose or direction, with no goal in view.

clue.text: Commentator's inclined to be fast

indicators.note: a commentator speaks, so the word is as heard rather than as written

parts.note: leant means leaned over, inclined

explanation.surface: A sports commentator tends to speak quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclined to be fast' reads as tending to speed; 'fast' is the Christian period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lent is the forty-day Christian season of fasting before Easter.

clue.text: Coach, according to linesman, always calling

parts.note: in American usage a railway coach is a car
a linesman here is a poet, writer of lines, and e'er is the poetic form of ever, always

explanation.surface: A football coach, so the linesman says, is forever shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linesman' looks like a match official; it is a poet, whose 'always' is E'ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is a profession or vocation, one's calling in life.

clue.text: Supplies more stilettos, say, behind woman's address

parts.note: behind as a noun is the rear
Ms is a form of address for a woman

explanation.surface: A shop stocks more high heels, worn behind by a smartly addressed woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Stilettos look like shoes, but here they are daggers: weapons, so supplying more is rearming.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearm is to supply with weapons again, and a stiletto is a slim dagger.

clue.text: Shackle males disrupting later broadcast

indicators.note: the males break into the middle of the other letters
broadcast means scattered, so the letters of later are thrown about

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male, so two males are MM

explanation.surface: Restrictions on men interfere with a later programme going out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scrambles the letters of later into TRAEL, and 'disrupting' breaks into it with the two males.
explanation.definitionFit: A trammel is a restraint or impediment, a shackle on free movement.

clue.text: See uniform of US academy soldiers

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British soldiers

explanation.surface: Look at the uniform worn by soldiers at an American military academy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a command to look; it is a bishop's see (diocese), and 'See uniform' is a bishop's regalia.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is the tall headdress a bishop wears as part of the vestments of office in a diocese.

clue.text: Betting rings to stay

indicators.note: the betting term surrounds, rings, the next word

parts.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds when a race begins

explanation.surface: Betting rings at the racecourse are told to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' looks like betting syndicates; it is a verb, the starting-price abbreviation encircling the word to.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop at a place is to stay there briefly.

clue.text: River sample from retired bacteriologist

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the sampled letters are read backwards
only a small run of letters is taken from inside bacteriologist

explanation.surface: A river sample is taken from a bacteriologist who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sample from' takes ERIOL from inside bACTERIOLogist; 'retired' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France.

clue.text: They curtailed training in outhouse, stretching back and bottom

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written before its tail is cut off

indicators.note: the training is placed in the middle of the outhouse
the outhouse is read backwards, from end to start

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: People cut short their exercise in a shed, stretching their backs and bottoms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' docks the last letter of They; 'stretching back' reverses the outhouse to DEHS, and 'in' puts the training inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The depths are the deepest part of something, its lowest point or bottom.

clue.text: Stashed aspirin all around — you might want to swallow them

definitions.text: you might want to swallow them

indicators.note: the letters are scattered all around, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Painkillers have been hidden everywhere, and you might need to take them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all around' is the anagram signal on STASHED ASPIRIN. The definition seems to mean pills; it is a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish pastries are sweet baked goods eaten, that is swallowed, as a treat.
